message.abstract: <jats:p>This work proposes an end-to-end defect detection framework for semiconductor wafers based on the Point Transformer architecture. The proposed model operates directly on image data represented as point sets, enabling robust handling of images at varying resolutions while also providing defect localization. Unlike conventional feature-extraction-based pipelines, the model is trained using a reconstruction-based learning strategy. This design allows training exclusively on normal wafer images, eliminating the need for defective samples. Since abnormal wafer data are inherently scarce, existing methods often rely on synthetic defect generation, which introduces strong domain dependencies and practical limitations. Our approach avoids this requirement entirely. The proposed framework also offers significant flexibility in resolution handling. Training can be performed on low-resolution images to reduce computational cost, while inference can be conducted on high-resolution images without architectural modification. Finally, the model directly identifies potential defect locations in image data, providing interpretable, practical outputs for real-world wafer inspection systems.</jats:p>
title: Reconstruction-based Wafer Anomaly Detection in Semiconductor Manufacturing with Point Transformers
